title: The Road to Reims
description: June-July 1429. After the victory at Orleans, Joan of Arc must escort the Dauphin Charles through English-held territory to the cathedral at Reims for his coronation. English garrisons at Troyes and Chalons block the route and can be fought or persuaded to surrender. Victory requires the Dauphin reaching Reims cathedral alive; his death means defeat.

anachronisms_found: English garrison of Troyes is built from CROSSBOWMAN and PIKEMAN only; the engine offers the Longbowman (and Man-at-Arms/Man-at-Arms line) which would be the obvious avoidable choice for a 1429 English garrison, and the crossbow-heavy roster actually reads as French
GAIA TREE_OAK x2880 on a 120x120 map turns the open chalk plains and vineyards of Champagne into dense forest
Reims Cathedral, the entire objective of the campaign, is represented only by a GAIA MONASTERY; a Wonder or a walled town centre was available and would have read far better
Player THREE 'English-loyal raiders' are CHAMPION + MILITIA, i.e. the plain infantry line, which gives no cultural read at all for Anglo-Burgundian routiers
